headline: Hotter inflation dents the ASX as Wall Street’s tech rally fades
paragraphs: Australian shares slipped on Wednesday as inflation picked up again. The ASX 200 closed down 0.4% at 8,692.4. It recovered the sharp dip that followed the inflation release, but weakness in miners and banks kept it in the red. Annual October inflation rose to 4.9% from 4.3% in September. Trimmed mean inflation, which strips out the biggest price swings, rose from 3.6% to 3.8%.

The Australian dollar’s jump was brief. CBA strategist Carol Kong said it rose towards 66.7 US cents on the inflation news before giving back the gain. By 5:39 pm Sydney, it was at 65.78 US cents, down 0.92% from MarketWatch’s previous close. Higher inflation can make near-term rate cuts less likely, but that wasn’t enough to keep the currency higher.

Wall Street’s Tuesday cash session was more divided than the S&P 500’s 0.50% fall to 7,201.09 suggests. The Nasdaq-100 slid 1.99% to 26,214.17 as AI stocks gave back some of Monday’s gains, while the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. The sell-off was concentrated in tech rather than shared across the whole market.

Gold and oil both weakened in Wednesday trading. Kitco’s spot gold bid was US$3,517.10 a troy ounce at 6:06 pm Sydney, down 1.07%. January Brent futures were down 1.50% at US$90.03 a barrel in a delayed 4:22 pm Sydney quote, giving back part of Tuesday’s rise. Reuters reported that expectations of ample supply outweighed concerns about Middle East disruptions. The next US tests are October PCE inflation and the second estimate of third-quarter GDP, both due at 12:30 am Thursday Sydney time.
